title: Why context is the missing piece in revenue automation
summary: See how Zoom Revenue Accelerator and Common Room help carry buyer context from signal to renewal in our recent webinar.
body_markdown:
A buyer joins your webinar and asks a sharp question. Ten minutes later, they're on your pricing page. Someone is leaning in.


So what happens next at your company?


Does that moment reach the rep who owns the account, with the who, the what, and the why attached? Or does it sit in one tool until the rep hears about it a week later? If they hear about it at all.


Erin Kriese and Jared Wexler opened our recent[Zoom Revenue Accelerator webinar](https://success.zoom.us/rec/share/J-urgP21Eg2-dDqn_ZMVjPkDNFU7zoedSSVvsxFtcxWRKWZyXh88kw-zbFtLoYC-.QwaSzbpOkXf9yrh0?recFileId=c87cb935-9cfc-407c-893f-bde551dc5470&pageType=web&autoplay=true) with exactly that question, as a live poll. "No judgment here," Erin told the audience. "Most of us are probably somewhere in the middle." She was right. Plenty of people said signals reach reps only "sometimes," usually because a colleague forwards them by hand. Others said signals get through, but the context falls off somewhere on the way.


That second answer is the one worth sitting with. The *why* behind it gets lost.

## Your team has plenty of automation. What it's missing is context.


Every quarter, revenue teams add more automations, like stalled deal alerts, forecast roll-ups or engagement sequences. Each one tends to solve a single scenario, sit apart from the others, and run a step behind what the buyer just did.


Meanwhile, many tools in the stack now ships its own AI for signals, enrichment, sequencing, or calling. Erin put it bluntly in the webinar: "Six sets of intelligence that don't share context are not an advantage. They're six more silos for your team to work through." Your buyer, meanwhile, still sees only fragments.


Picture that fragmented workflow. The signal fires on Tuesday, and the rep finds out next Monday. Discovery happens in one system while the follow-up gets drafted in another. Notes get retyped into the CRM, or they don't, and quietly the record stops being true.


Then comes the forecast, assembled last from whatever survived the handoffs. Forecasting at many teams is "going from gut feeling," they said in the webinar. It isn't codified across the team, and it doesn't draw on any central context layer.


Who stitches all of this together? Your reps. They've become the integration layer, and people don't scale the way systems do.


## So what does building on context look like?


That's where the webinar gets practical. In about 20 minutes, Erin and Jared go from the problem to a working answer. You'll follow one buyer, Laura, from a quiet pricing page visit to a booked meeting. All without reps having to hunt for her signal along the way.


You'll also get a 4-question test you can run on the automation in your stack this week. And you'll see how an AI agent can spot a stalled deal and get it moving again before the rep even notices it went quiet.


Many teams already have the signals. Getting them to the right person with the story attached is the hard part, and the recording can give you deeper insights.
